intro: There was no ICO for ERG. Every ERG enters circulation according to a fixed schedule, written into the protocol from day one: each new block releases a set amount of ERG, and that amount shrinks over time until it reaches zero. In total there will only ever be {{max}} ERG.

stats.lockedSub: Paid out to miners over time

schedule.title: The emission schedule
schedule.rule1: {{rate}} ERG per block for the first {{period}} blocks (~2 years at 2-minute blocks).
schedule.rule2: After that, every {{epoch}} blocks (~3 months) the emission drops by {{drop}} ERG.
schedule.rule3: Once it hits 0 — at block {{end}} — new emission stops.
schedule.chartTitle: ERG created per block, by height
schedule.chartLabel: ERG emitted per block by height
schedule.p2: Unlike Bitcoin, which abruptly “halves” every 4 years, Ergo's curve steps down in small, even stairs. And instead of stretching over more than a century, all ERG is emitted in about 8 years — after which network security relies on transaction fees (and re-emission, see below).

treasury.title: The treasury share
treasury.p1: In the early years, part of each block's scheduled emission went to a treasury to fund development: {{t1}} ERG/block for the first {{period}} blocks, then {{t2}} and {{t3}} ERG over the next two epochs. Miners received the rest ({{miner}} ERG/block) from the emission box. The treasury's share never passed through the emission box: it was set aside at genesis in a separate treasury box holding 4,330,791.5 ERG, roughly what these per-block amounts add up to, and a vesting contract released it gradually. From block {{from}} onwards, the entire emission goes to miners.
treasury.announcement: The original announcement, Ergo's emission curve (May 2019), explains the split: the treasury gets 4.43% of all emitted ERG to fund development, promotion and events, and to swap the pre-launch EFYT tokens for ERG. That swap ran 1:1 until 1 July 2021: the treasury paid out 1,782,615 ERG, and 188,330 EFYT were never claimed. Before launch, EFYT had been airdropped to the community, used to pay developers (about 150,000 EFYT in 2018) and other costs, and 500,000 EFYT were sold to three private investors. Since any holder could swap, part of the treasury's ERG was in effect spent, and sold, before mainnet launched.
treasury.p2: The treasury box's contract checks two things: the box can only be spent if at least the not-yet-due part of the schedule stays locked in it, and the spender must satisfy the condition stored in R4, which at launch was a 2-of-3 multisignature of Ergo Foundation members. See the ErgoDocs FAQ for the genesis boxes, the Ergo Foundation Treasury page for how the funds were spent, and foundationScript in the sigmastate-interpreter source for the contract.

eip27.title: EIP-27: re-emission
eip27.p1: The original schedule had a problem: emission ends fairly early, while transaction fees might not be enough to keep miners around. EIP-27, activated by a soft fork at block {{height}} (in 2022), “saves” part of today's reward to pay it out gradually in the future:
eip27.li1: If the block's emission is ≥ 15 ERG: 12 ERG is locked into the re-emission contract.
eip27.li2: If it is below 15 ERG: (emission − 3) ERG is locked, so the miner always gets at least 3 ERG.
eip27.li3: After emission ends (block {{start}}), the contract pays {{per}} ERG per block back to miners until it runs dry.
eip27.p2: In total, EIP-27 locks about {{total}} ERG. Paid out at {{per}} ERG per block, that lasts roughly another {{blocks}} blocks — until around block {{end}} (≈ {{year}}). The total supply doesn't change; only the timing of when ERG reaches miners is stretched out.

miner.title: How much does a miner actually get?
miner.text: Take block {{h}}: {{e}} ERG emitted, {{l}} ERG locked, and the miner receives {{m}} ERG + transaction fees. Open any block to see the emission, reemitted and reward fields.

outro: Want the numbers at a specific height? Use the <calc>emission calculator</calc>. The dates above are estimates based on the average block time since launch (a little over 2 minutes); real timing can drift by a few weeks.
